definition: Audio samples per second: 8 kHz (telephony), 16 kHz (standard ASR), 24-48 kHz (TTS and music).
details: Audio samples per second: 8 kHz (telephony), 16 kHz (standard ASR), 24-48 kHz (TTS and music). Mismatched sample rates between training and inference are a classic silent quality killer.

explainer.lead: Sample rate is the number of audio samples taken per second. It matters because mismatches between training and inference rates can silently degrade quality.

tiers.eli5: Like how many snapshots per second a camera takes of a sound wave — more snapshots capture finer detail.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick 8 kHz for telephony, 16 kHz for standard ASR, and 24-48 kHz for TTS and music, and must resample consistently. The classic pitfall is a silent quality killer: training and inference rates that do not match.
tiers.paperLevel: Measured in hertz: audio samples per second. Common settings are 8 kHz telephony, 16 kHz standard ASR, and 24-48 kHz TTS and music; the rate bounds the representable frequency content.

explainer.example: An ASR model trained on 16 kHz audio fed 8 kHz input at inference will produce degraded transcriptions unless resampled first.
